title: Metric Critique: Match Volume vs Match Rate
scenario: The BooedUp product team wants to measure whether the new AI Type Score model is improving mutual attraction outcomes. A stakeholder proposes tracking 'Total Matches Created Per Week' as the primary metric.
prompt: The stakeholder argues that 'Total Matches Created Per Week' directly measures whether users are forming more romantic connections. What is wrong with this metric? Propose a better alternative in one sentence.
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Example format: 'Should be normalized. [Better Metric Name] is better.'
expected_themes: not normalized per active user or per interaction
absolute count masks underlying rate changes
mutual match rate is the correct proxy
reference_answer: Should be normalized per interaction initiated. Mutual Match Rate (matches per like/wink sent) is better.

grading_rubric.description: Answer states the metric is not normalized (per user, per interaction, or per cohort size)
Proposes a denominator: matches per active user, matches per interaction sent, or mutual match rate
Explains why absolute count can grow while quality/efficiency declines (e.g., more users but worse match rate)

hints: Think about what happens if the user base doubles but match quality stays flat.
Consider whether you care about total volume or efficiency per interaction.
What denominator would isolate the Type Score model's impact from user growth?
common_mistakes: Proposing 'Matches Per User' without specifying active users only (includes dormant accounts)
Suggesting median instead of mean (this is a count normalization problem, not an outlier problem)
Focusing on time lag instead of the missing denominator
